WHY THE MIX IS 100% EQUITY/ETF. config/strategy.md says a Sunday run should lean on crypto and event contracts. Both were checked and both produced nothing. Crypto: CoinGecko spot works, but `history` fails on every source (Yahoo 429, nasdaq returns no rows for crypto, no twelvedata/alphavantage key), so there is no ATR, no 20/50-day and no 90-day range for any coin — and the crypto swing stop floor is 2.5 ATR, so no stop could be placed from real structure. Event contracts: Kalshi search returns count 0 for CPI, Bitcoin, interest rate and government shutdown; the only 'Fed' hits are tennis markets matching the substring inside 'Federico', all with null prices. An event-contract thesis requires the market's implied probability against mine, and without a fetched price that is a fabricated number. This is the single biggest limitation of the run and it is a tooling outcome, not a judgement that nothing was out there. 

ONE DATA ERROR FOUND AND CORRECTED. finnhub's earnings calendar had GE Aerospace reporting 2026-10-19 BMO; GE's own investor-relations events page says 2026-10-20, 07:30 ET, corroborated by TipRanks ('Confirmed') and MarketBeat. This changed the recommendation: the first GE write-up said the print lands before Monday's open and so no action was available, when in fact the reader has all of Monday to act. UNP (2026-10-22 07:45) and ABT (2026-10-21 BMO) were then second-sourced to company releases and both CONFIRMED. So 1 of 4 verified dates was wrong, and it was the most consequential one. FCX (2026-10-27) and HII (2026-10-29) carry finnhub's date unverified — treat them as approximate to within a day and re-confirm before acting. 

TEN VALIDATION FLAGS, ALL DELIBERATE. The research phase recomputed every ratio against the floors and I recomputed all 17 independently from the fetched ATRs; the two agree exactly. Each flag below is the recommendation rather than a mistake, and a red team applying the floors mechanically would make the book worse:
  (1) HII 1.68 and BCC 1.31 R:R against the 2.5 long-term floor. THE FAILURE IS THE RECOMMENDATION — it is the stated reason HII is halved with its target marked down from 430.00 (25.63x trailing earnings, never defended) to 335.60 (20x), and the reason BCC is closed outright. Raising either target to clear the floor would re-introduce the undefended multiple being withdrawn. Both are published rather than dropped because the instruction — close BCC, halve HII — is the deliverable; if enforcement demotes them to the watchlist, those instructions still stand and are the reason for the demotion.
  (2) SMMT win probability 0.18 vs a 0.313 break-even, SNX 0.22 vs 0.325, BCC 0.25 vs 0.433 — negative expectancy, on purpose. These are the three positions being exited (two held to their stops, one closed). A stated win probability below the break-even hit rate is the honest claim for a trade expected to lose; inflating it to clear check_expectancy is exactly the numbers-nudged-until-they-passed failure this report has already shipped once. DO NOT RAISE THESE.
  (3) XLE 1.20 ATR and NKE 0.98 ATR entry-to-stop, flagged as sub-floor — a measurement artefact. In both cases the stop is now on the PROFITABLE side of the entry (XLE long, entry 63.90, stop 65.50; NKE short, entry 38.40, stop 39.60), so risk measured from entry is negative. Forward risk from spot is 2.06 ATR for XLE (clears the 1.8 ETF floor) and 2.01 ATR for NKE (clears the 2.0 stock floor). Widening these back toward the entry would hand back realised gains on two winning positions, which is the opposite of what the floor is for. Measure from spot, not entry.
  (4) SNX 1.82, FCX 1.84 and CEG 1.32 ATR stops, inside the 2.0 stock floor — inherited, not chosen today. All three were published that way before today and all three are filled, so the entry is a fact and the stop cannot be re-placed. Three sub-floor stops among 19 open rows is a finding about how this book was published, and it is recorded as one.

TWO PATTERNS WORTH SIZING AGAINST. First, eight of the fourteen swing ratios land between 2.00 and 2.19 against a 2.0 floor (TLT exactly 2.00, GE 2.06, LULU 2.07, SNX 2.08, STLD 2.12, FCX 2.12, CEG 2.18, SMMT 2.19). That cluster is precisely the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar, and it is named here rather than explained away. The mitigating fact is real but partial: every one of those levels was set on an earlier date on a now-filled position, so the clustering was inherited by today's run rather than manufactured by it. It still says this book was built close to the line. Second, the correlation cap in config/strategy.md is 3 ideas per driver and this book is well past it — GE, STLD, FCX, UNP, BCC, XLE and HII are seven tickets on one cyclical-industrial bet, and TLT, IYR, CEG, BCC and XLF are five rows turning on the same rate path. Both breaches are inherited from open positions rather than opened today, and they are the reason no new energy, steel, rail, copper, aerospace or rate-driven idea was pursued even where the setup looked reasonable. One idea was declined on this ground alone (a short-utilities trade, which is also the XLU short already opened 2026-09-24 and stopped out 2026-10-06).

ONE DECLARED CONFLICT. This report is short REITs (IYR) on a credit thesis while long the banks that lend against that credit (XLF). The reconciliation is composition — XLF is weighted to money-centre, insurance and payments earnings rather than the regional CRE book — and it is only a partial answer, which is why XLF stays at conviction 3, is capped, and must not be added to. The falsification test is dated: if the 2026-10-20/10-21 bank prints show reserve builds at the money centres too, the distinction fails and XLF closes.

FILL RATE. Five of nine pending ideas never filled and the move happened anyway — four were entries set below the market on longs or above it on shorts. RED TEAM (phase 2c). Cut 9 of 17; 8 remain. Three distinct reasons, and only one of them is the validator agreeing with itself.

(1) FOUR ROWS WERE EXIT INSTRUCTIONS PUBLISHED AS BUY PITCHES. BCC said 'close the full position' in a `buy` row with an 88.43 target; SNX and SMMT both said 'let the stop execute' from entries that are 5.1% and 16.9% away from the market; HII said 'halve it' at a self-declared 1.68:1 against a 2.5 floor. All four lose money on their own stated hit rates or ratios. The instructions were good and they are preserved verbatim on the watchlist — what came out is the pretence that they were recommendations to open something.

(2) TWO RATIOS MEASURED NOTHING BECAUSE THE ENTRY IS HISTORY. XLE's 4.12:1 divides 6.60 of upside by a 1.60 LOCKED-IN GAIN, because the stop was raised above the filled entry; the direction check fails for the same reason. NKE's 0.98 ATR 'noise stop' is 2.01 ATR above spot, tightened to protect a realised gain. Both amendments are correct trade management and both are unpublishable as reward-to-risk pitches, so they move to the watchlist carrying their instructions. This is a gap in the schema, not an error by the author: there is no way to express a protected winner as an entry/target/stop triple.

(3) THREE JUDGEMENT CUTS. TLT's 2.00:1 sits exactly on the floor only because the target is 0.73 below the 90-day low — at the real range low it is 1.65:1 — and the position is flat after four weeks of exactly the backdrop it wants, on a trade it concedes is the most crowded in macro. FCX is the fourth correlated industrial-demand row against a cap of three, on a sub-floor 1.84 ATR stop with momentum already below both averages.

THE SAME TARGET PATTERN RUNS THROUGH ALL FOUR SHORTS. IYR, LULU and TLT each clear 2.0:1 only by projecting past the 90-day range extreme, while each one's own scale plan names that extreme as where to take profit. At the structural level they are 1.73, 0.90 and 1.65 to 1. TLT is cut; IYR and LULU are kept with the finding written into `key_risk`, because their relative-strength and macro legs stand on their own. The longs do not have this problem — every long target sits at or inside its 90-day range.

watchlist.note: TESTED AND REJECTED. The macro case was good — 14+ regionals report 2026-10-19 to 10-21 and a +0.35 curve with a 5.10% 10-year is a net-interest-margin tailwind — and every fetched confirmation contradicted it: 4 of 4 below their 50-day, 4 of 4 with zero open-market insider buying and net selling (ZION -$6.58M, EWBC -$12.11M, WAL -$3.78M, FITB -$1.31M), two with deteriorating revisions. ZION beat by 65% last quarter and still sits near its 90-day low of 60.76. The inference is the valuable part: the credit channel is dominating the NIM channel, because a curve steepening from the LONG end at 5.10% raises funding costs and stresses commercial real estate at once. That corroborates the IYR short rather than arguing for a bank long.

watchlist.note: RED TEAM CUT from rank 14. The 2.00:1 ratio lands exactly on the floor and it is there by construction: the 75.70 target sits 0.73 BELOW the 90-day low of 76.43, and measured against that actual range low the trade is 1.65:1 and under the floor. That is the targets-nudged-until-they-pass pattern this phase exists to catch, and it is the third short in this report built the same way — IYR and LULU are kept with the finding disclosed on each, because both have something else holding them up and this one does not. The macro reading is genuinely well measured, and the trade still has not worked: open since 2026-09-24 and flat at -0.2% after four weeks in which the 10-year sat at 5.10% with the curve positively sloped — the exact backdrop the thesis asks for. A position that does not pay while it is right is a priced one, and the row itself calls short duration the most crowded macro trade of the cycle, with negative carry and borrow on top. ACTION WHILE OPEN: hold the 82.00 stop; do not add.
